desk.headline: Sales up 0.4% to $1.37bn but Q4 profit fell 28% on a lower gross margin; full-year net income up 16%; no guidance
results: Fourth-quarter sales edged up to $1.374bn from $1.368bn, with 13 weeks in both quarters.
Gross margin slipped to 23.9% from 24.5% while operating costs rose to $303.9m, cutting operating income to $24.5m from $35.0m.
Net income fell to $18.5m ($0.97 per diluted Class A share) from $25.7m ($1.35).
Full year: sales $5.42bn, gross margin 24.4% (23.9% last year) and net income $96.8m, up from $83.6m.
Cash rose to $459m and debt fell to $497m; FY26 capex was $100.6m (FY25: $114.5m), and the $150m credit line was undrawn apart from a $0.9m letter of credit.

guidance.summary: Ingles gives no financial guidance. It noted three stores closed since Hurricane Helene are expected to reopen in 2027 or 2028.

call.source: No call coverage found (the company does not usually hold a results call)

watch: Whether gross margin recovers after the year-on-year dip in the fourth quarter.
Sales trends as hurricane-closed stores reopen in 2027 and 2028.
Use of the growing cash balance and further debt reduction.
